content: """Forced-mate search (used by the puzzle mode, V7).
``can_mate_in(board, n)`` answers: can the side to move force checkmate in at
most ``n`` of its **own** moves, whatever the opponent replies?
``find_mates(board, n)`` returns every first move that does so — a puzzle is
valid when this list has exactly one element (the solution).
Detection reuses the alpha-beta negamax: a mate delivered by the side to move
within ``2n`` plies scores ``>= MATE_SCORE``, which prunes the tree heavily.
def can_mate_in(board: Board, n: int) -> bool:
"""True if the side to move can force checkmate in <= n of its own moves."""
def find_mates(board: Board, n: int) -> list[Move]:
"""All first moves of the side to move that force mate in <= n moves."""

# i.e. the child's negamax score must be <= -MATE_SCORE at depth 2n-2.

"""Smallest n <= max_n such that the side to move can force mate in n, else None."""

Used by the puzzle mode: after the solver's move, the computer plays the
